facts.statement: The genus Archaeorhynchus was first reported in 2005 by researchers Zhou and Zhang.
facts.quote: A fossil of its only known species, Archaeorhynchus spathula, was first reported in 2005 by Zhou & Zhang

facts.statement: Archaeorhynchus is a genus of beaked avialans that lived during the Early Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: Archaeorhynchus (meaning "ancient snout") is a genus of beaked avialans from the early Cretaceous period.

facts.statement: The type specimen of Archaeorhynchus spathula was found in the Yixian Formation at Yixian, Liaoning province, China.
facts.quote: A fossil of its only known species, Archaeorhynchus spathula, was first reported in 2005 by Zhou & Zhang to have been found in Yixian Formation rocks at Yixian, Liaoning province, China

facts.statement: The age range for Archaeorhynchus spathula is estimated to be between 125 and 120 million years ago.
facts.quote: These deposits are 120 million years old, whereas the original specimen was 125 million years old, meaning the age range for this species is 125-120Ma.

facts.statement: Fossils of Archaeorhynchus preserve feathers on the neck, head, and tail regions.
facts.quote: The fossils preserved feathers associated with the neck, head and tail regions.

facts.statement: Grooves and foramina on the jaw tips suggest Archaeorhynchus supported a horny bill.
facts.quote: The fossils also show grooves and openings/ holes (foramina) on the tips of the upper and lower jaws, suggesting that it supported a horny bill.

facts.statement: Archaeorhynchus was a medium-sized avialan measuring approximately 20 cm in length, 15.5 cm in hip height, and weighing 275 grams.
facts.quote: Archaeorhynchus was a medium-sized avialan, measuring about 20 cm long, hip height of 15.5 cm, and weight of 275 g.

facts.statement: The finger bones of Archaeorhynchus show a phalangeal formula of 2-3-2.
facts.quote: The forelimbs also preserved the major and minor metacarpals as well as the finger bones showing a phalangeal formula of 2-3-2.

facts.statement: Scientists hypothesize that Archaeorhynchus had an herbivorous diet based on the presence of numerous gastroliths in all known specimens.
facts.quote: Scientists have hypothesized that the Archaeorhynchus had an herbivorous diet, due to the large numbers of gastroliths (stomach stones) found in the gut of all known specimens.

facts.statement: A 2021 study suggests Archaeorhynchus probably demonstrated flight soon after birth.
facts.quote: A 2021 study on a juvenile specimen shows that, much like Enantiornithes and megapodes, Archaeorhynchus probably demonstrated flight soon after birth.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis indicates that Archaeorhynchus is most closely related to ornithurines.
facts.quote: Phylogenetic analysis conducted by Zhou & Zhang indicated that Archaeorhynchus was most closely related to ornithurines.

facts.statement: Archaeorhynchus is classified within the unranked order Euornithes.
Archaeorhynchus lived from the Barremian to the Aptian stages, between 125.77 and 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Aptian (125.77 to 113.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: It is debated whether the gastroliths were swallowed accidentally or intentionally, though high numbers suggest the latter.
facts.quote: High numbers of these gastroliths suggest that they were not swallowed accidentally.
